title: Phenoxide resonance
back: Charge spread over O and the ortho and para carbons: phenoxide is stabilised, so phenol (p$K_a$ 10) is far more acidic than ethanol (15.9).

title: Propene to two alcohols
back: Acid hydration goes through a carbocation; hydroboration–oxidation does not.

title: Kolbe's reaction
back: Product: salicylic acid. Phenoxide is reactive enough to be attacked by the weak electrophile CO₂.

title: Reimer–Tiemann reaction
back: Product: salicylaldehyde. Puts –CHO at the ortho position.

title: Williamson synthesis
back: A tertiary halide gives an alkene instead. Put the bulky group on the alkoxide.

title: Ethanol + conc. H₂SO₄
back: Higher temperature: elimination (alkene). Lower temperature, excess alcohol: ether.

title: Anisole + HI
back: The O–aryl bond has partial double-bond character and never breaks, so iodobenzene is never formed.

title: Acid strength order
back: Phenol dissolves in NaOH but does not release $\ce{CO2}$ from $\ce{NaHCO3}$.

title: Kolbe vs Reimer–Tiemann
back: Kolbe: phenoxide + $\ce{CO2}$ → salicylic acid. Reimer–Tiemann: phenol + chloroform + NaOH → salicylaldehyde.

title: Cumene process
back: The industrial route to phenol; acetone is the by-product.

title: Lucas test
back: Tertiary in a Twinkle, Secondary in Some minutes, Primary Plays dead.

title: Why ethanol boils higher than its ether isomer
back: Alcohols form intermolecular hydrogen bonds through O–H; ethers cannot. Both still dissolve in water about equally.

title: ortho- vs para-nitrophenol
back: Intramolecular H-bonding makes o-nitrophenol volatile in steam, so the isomers are separated by steam distillation.

title: Ethanol by fermentation
back: Both enzymes come from yeast; no air. Denatured alcohol: ethanol made undrinkable with CuSO₄ and pyridine.
